chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

"Whoever sells a good and says, 'Its price is such-and-such cash on the spot, and its price is such-and-such deferred; take whichever price you wish, and make the transaction one,' then he is not entitled to anything but the lesser of the two, even if it is the deferred price."
He (peace be upon him) also said: "Whoever bargains with two prices, one immediate and the other deferred, he must specify one of them before the transaction."

And with this chain, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (may God's prayers be upon him) ruled in the case of a man whom a group of people ordered to buy a camel for them with cash, and to add to that price as deferred payment; so he bought a camel for them, and some of them were with him, and he prevented him from taking from them above the price of the camel as deferred payment.

key_terms.يَدًا بِيَدٍ: Cash on the spot / Immediate payment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a sale where the seller offers both a cash price and a deferred price?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the prohibition of *Gharar* (uncertainty) in mixed-price sales, establishing that if a seller offers a choice between cash and deferred prices in a single contract, the lower price prevails to ensure clarity. It further illustrates the practical application of these rules in brokerage (*Wakalah*), where the agent must explicitly define the payment structure before concluding the transaction. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between valid conditional sales and those void due to ambiguity.
